units.sentence: Every card uses the same fields, and one rule sets every evidence label.
"Supported" means a record that settles the point backs the claim.
For what a rule says, that record is the rule's own text.
For money, needs or effects, it is a county record written by someone other than the people making the claim...
"Uncertain" means only statements or requests by the people making the claim back it, no record settles it, or the key document isn't out yet.
"A values question" means that part of the claim is about what is fair or right, not mainly about facts.
When a card makes more than one claim, each part gets its own label.
A claim type says "with a values question" when the card also asks what is fair or right, and the label names that question.
"Documented" means a real person or body made the argument, and we cite where.
Cards are paired by topic: who drafts (1 and 2), requests and openness (3 and 4), then timing (5) and funding (6).
The first pair starts with the case for the current process, and the second with the case against it; the order is not a ranking.
